sentences.text: Shri Akhlesh Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the appellants  Shri Naresh Singh Tomar- Advocate for respondent No.3.

ORDER Heard on IA No.6047/2025 , an application for exemption of notice to respondent No.1 and 2.
2.
On due consideration and for the reasons mentioned in the application, IA No.6047/2025 is allowed.
Service of notice on respondent No.1 and 2 is dispensed with at the risk of the appellants.

3. This appeal filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of award dated 26/07/2023 passed by I MACT, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 533/2019 on account of inadequacy of the compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
4.. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute, however, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.
5. As per the finding of the Tribunal, in the case of death of Sachin, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.10,09,857/- with interest from filing of petition till its realization.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17056 2 MA-3322-2025 6.

Learned counsel for the appellants contends that the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal accepting earning of the deceased as Rs. 6100/- per month is inadequate looking to the fact that he was working as labour.

However, accepting the earning as Rs 7325/- per month and adding future Savayi Lal vs Deendayal on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21311813/
1 prospects, applying adequate multiplier, the reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Tribunal.

8..After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal for calculating the compensation amount is on lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under as per Minimum Wages Act :-
 Monthly Income 7325X12=
 87,900/-
 Multiplier of 17 87,900 X 17=14,94,300/-
 Personal Expenses 1/2 14,94,300 X 1/2= 7,47,150  7,47,150/- +2,98,860=
 Future Prospect 40%
 10,46,010/-
 Consortium 44,000/-
 Funeral 16,500/-
 Loss of Estate 16,500/-
 Medical Expenses 61,777/-
 Total - 11,
 Tribunal awarded  10,
 compensation  Enhanced compensation  1,7  amount 9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs 11,84,787/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.10,09,857/-.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17056 3 MA-3322-2025 Rs.1,74,930/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10.
With the aforesaid modification, compensation amount is enhanced to a sum of Rs. 1,74,930/- -.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization .
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
